heard: One tiny moon looks like a jigsaw puzzle glued back together. When Voyager 2 reached Uranus in 1986, scientists expected its moon Miranda to be a boring ice ball. Instead, they found a Frankenstein world of mismatched geological blocks and a massive V-shaped scar. Miranda's surface features Verona ropes, a staggering cliff reaching up to 12 miles deep. That is 12 times deeper than the Grand Canyon, on a world barely the size of Texas. One leading theory suggests this chaotic moon was shattered by impacts multiple times before reassembling. Alternatively, extreme tidal heating from Uranus might have churned the moon's icy interior into these bizarre shapes. Since we have only photographed its southern half, the rest of the jigsaw puzzle remains a mystery.
